title: Property B: The Convex Tradeoff Behind the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan Flip Rate
description: The open question property-b-first-moment-oq-03 asks to sharpen Erdős's 1963 bound m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1) to the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan m(k) = Ω(2^k·√(k/log k)) via the asymmetric/recoloring refinement of the first-moment argument. Three sibling entries settled the NEGATIVE half (asymmetry oq-03-oq-01 and independent/product-space recoloring oq-03-oq-03 are both worthless) and the deterministic recoloring core (oq-03-oq-02), pinning the RS gain entirely on the conditional, order-dependent recoloring of only the dangerous (already-monochromatic) edges. This entry supplies the two QUANTITATIVE facts the negatives could not reach. (1) Gain: under conditional recoloring a dangerous k-edge survives in its original color with probability survivesOrig p k = (1−p)^k, which is STRICTLY < 1 for every flip rate p ∈ (0,1] and k ≥ 1 — the positive counterpart to the product-model factor-1 inertness; it strictly lowers the expected number of surviving dangerous edges below the Erdős baseline m·2^(1-k). (2) Optimization engine: bounding the gain by (1−p)^k ≤ e^{−kp} and the recoloring loss linearly by c·k·p gives the strictly convex tradeoff G(p) = e^{−kp} + c·k·p, whose minimum over p is the closed form c·(1 − log c), ATTAINED at the small flip rate p* = −(log c)/k. This log(1/c)/k scaling of the optimizer is exactly the mechanism producing the RS √(k/log k) improvement. 8 theorems, 3 defs, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

meta.author: Lean Genius

mathlibDependencies.description: x + 1 ≤ exp x — the tangent-line bound. Used both for 1 − p ≤ e^{−p} (linearizing the gain) and, after the substitution s = kp + log c, as the single inequality from which the convex optimum c·(1 − log c) follows.

Exponential–logarithm algebra: exp(log c) = c (c > 0), exp(a − b) = exp a / exp b, and exp(k·x) = (exp x)^k, used to evaluate the tradeoff at the optimum and to raise 1 − p ≤ e^{−p} to the k-th power.
Monotonicity of x ↦ x^n on [0,∞): gives (1−p)^k < 1 for 0 < p ≤ 1 (strict gain), (1−p)^k ≤ 1, and (1−p)^k ≤ (e^{−p})^k.
a ≤ b / c ↔ a·c ≤ b for c > 0 — clears the denominator after rewriting exp(−(x+log c)) = e^{−x}/c, reducing the optimum bound to a linear inequality closed by nlinarith.

originalContributions: survivesOrig_lt_one: conditional recoloring strictly helps — a dangerous k-edge survives in its original color with probability (1−p)^k < 1 for every flip rate p ∈ (0,1] and k ≥ 1, the positive quantitative counterpart to the product-model inertness of oq-03-oq-03 (where the analogous factor is identically 1).

expSurvivors_cond_lt_baseline: the expected number of surviving dangerous edges m·2^(1-k)·(1−p)^k is strictly below the Erdős baseline m·2^(1-k) for any positive flip rate — conditional recoloring beats the first moment (loss term aside).
survivesOrig_le_exp: the gain term is linearized, (1−p)^k ≤ e^{−kp}, via 1 − p ≤ e^{−p} raised to the k-th power.

tradeoff_ge_optimum: the central optimization lemma — for every flip rate p the convex tradeoff proxy G(p) = e^{−kp} + c·k·p is bounded below by the closed-form optimum c·(1 − log c). Proof reduces, after s = kp + log c, to the single tangent-line inequality 1 − s ≤ e^{−s}.

tradeoff_eq_at_optimum / optimum_flip_rate: tightness — G attains c·(1 − log c) exactly at k·p = −log c, i.e. the small flip rate p* = −(log c)/k = log(1/c)/k, the optimizer scaling behind the RS √(k/log k) gain.
meta.assumptions: None. All 7 theorems fully proved with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (no native_decide; the proofs are real analysis via Real.add_one_le_exp, exp/log algebra, pow-monotonicity, and nlinarith). #print axioms on the main results reports only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Probabilities are modeled as real-valued functions (the standard first-moment idiom of the sibling entries), not via a measure space. The loss term is modeled linearly as c·k·p with c a positive constant; deriving the genuine loss coefficient from the conditional model, the union bound over m edges, and the final √(k/log k) asymptotic remain open (see open questions).

overview.historicalContext: Property B (Erdős 1963) asks for the minimum number m(k) of edges in a k-uniform hypergraph that is not 2-colorable. The first-moment method gives m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1). Radhakrishnan and Srinivasan (2000) improved this to m(k) = Ω(2^k·√(k/log k)) by a two-stage argument: color uniformly, then recolor the vertices of the surviving monochromatic ('dangerous') edges, in a random order, each with a small probability p ≈ (log k)/k. The √(k/log k) factor emerges from balancing two competing effects — recoloring repairs dangerous edges (gain) but creates new ones (loss) — and optimizing the flip rate. The sibling entries proved the easy shortcuts inert; this entry formalizes the actual quantitative levers: the per-edge gain factor and the convex gain/loss tradeoff whose optimum is the small flip rate driving the improvement.
overview.problemStatement: Quantify the conditional recoloring step that the sibling negatives isolated as the sole source of the RS gain. (1) Show a dangerous k-edge survives with probability (1−p)^k, strictly below 1 for any positive flip rate — conditional recoloring genuinely helps. (2) Model the gain/loss balance as the convex proxy G(p) = e^{−kp} + c·k·p, and prove its minimum over the flip rate is the closed form c·(1 − log c), attained at the small rate p* = −(log c)/k — the optimizer whose log(1/c)/k scaling underlies the RS √(k/log k) factor.
overview.text: The analytic ACT engine for the open question property-b-first-moment-oq-03: the positive quantitative gain of conditional recoloring plus the convex optimization selecting the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan flip rate.
overview.proofStrategy: Two threads. GAIN: survivesOrig p k = (1−p)^k; strict improvement survivesOrig_lt_one is pow_lt_one₀ on 0 ≤ 1−p < 1; expSurvivors_cond_lt_baseline multiplies through by the positive Erdős baseline via mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left; survivesOrig_le_exp raises 1 − p ≤ e^{−p} (from Real.add_one_le_exp at −p) to the k-th power with pow_le_pow_left₀ and Real.exp_nat_mul. OPTIMIZATION: tradeoff_ge_optimum proves e^{−kp} + c·k·p ≥ c·(1 − log c) for all p. Writing x = k·p, substitute and use exp(−(x+log c)) = e^{−x}/c (Real.exp_sub, Real.exp_log); the tangent-line bound Real.add_one_le_exp at −(x+log c), after clearing the denominator with le_div_iff₀ and nlinarith, is exactly the claim — equivalently exp(−s) ≥ 1 − s with s = x + log c. tradeoff_eq_at_optimum evaluates G at k·p = −log c to c·(1 − log c) (exp(log c) = c), proving the lower bound is attained; optimum_flip_rate records p* = −(log c)/k.
keyInsights: Conditional recoloring (flip only dangerous-edge vertices) has survival factor (1−p)^k < 1 for any p > 0 — strictly better than the product model's inert factor 1, converting the sibling negative into a positive gain.
The √(k/log k) improvement is not free: flipping vertices creates new dangerous edges, a loss term growing with p, so the unconstrained optimum p = 1/2 is unavailable.
Bounding gain by e^{−kp} and loss by c·k·p yields a strictly convex tradeoff G(p) whose minimum is the clean closed form c·(1 − log c).
The minimizer is a SMALL flip rate p* = −(log c)/k = log(1/c)/k — this log/k scaling is precisely the source of the RS √(k/log k) gain.
The whole optimization collapses, after one substitution, to the single elementary inequality 1 − s ≤ e^{−s} (Real.add_one_le_exp): the convex envelope is a one-line tangent-line argument.
prerequisites: The first-moment / probabilistic method and Erdős's m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1)
The Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan recoloring (alteration) argument at a high level
Convexity and the tangent-line bound 1 + x ≤ e^x
Elementary exponential/logarithm algebra (exp(log c) = c, exp(a−b) = exp a / exp b)

This file formalises the two facts the negatives could not reach: the gain — a dangerous edge survives with probability (1−p)^k, strictly < 1 for p ∈ (0,1] — and the convex tradeoff G(p) = e^{−kp} + c·k·p whose minimum c·(1 − log c) is attained at the small flip rate p* = −(log c)/k, the log(1/c)/k scaling behind RS's √(k/log k) improvement. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 179 lines, 8 theorems and 3 definitions supplying the quantitative engine of the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan program for Property B: conditional recoloring strictly lowers a dangerous k-edge's survival probability to (1−p)^k < 1 (and the expected survivor count below the Erdős baseline), and the convex gain/loss tradeoff G(p) = e^{−kp} + c·k·p attains its minimum c·(1 − log c) at the small flip rate p* = −(log c)/k.
conclusion.implications: This is the positive complement to the three sibling entries: where they proved the asymmetry and product-space recoloring shortcuts inert, this entry exhibits the genuine lever — conditional recoloring strictly helps — and formalizes the convex optimization whose log(1/c)/k optimizer is the mechanism behind the RS √(k/log k) improvement. The optimization lemma (tradeoff_ge_optimum together with tradeoff_eq_at_optimum) is a reusable, self-contained closed-form minimum for any gain/loss balance of the form e^{−kp} + c·k·p.
openQuestions: Derive the genuine loss coefficient c from the conditional, order-dependent recoloring model (the rate at which flipping a vertex of one dangerous edge creates a new monochromatic edge), replacing the linear placeholder c·k·p with the true second-moment-style bound.

Assemble the union bound over the m edges and substitute the optimum flip rate p* = −(log c)/k to extract a genuine m(k) = Ω(2^k·√(k/log k)) asymptotic — the remaining real-analysis bookkeeping (roadmap steps 1–3).

Lift the real-valued first-moment idiom to a measure-theoretic conditional probability space in Mathlib (PMF / product measures with conditioning) to make the two-stage recoloring rigorous as a probability model rather than a real-valued proxy.
